title: Dual-Tier Cyberattack Detection for Distributed Energy Resource Aggregators
abstract: As distributed energy resources (DERs) and DER aggregators are integrated into distribution systems, the attack surface of critical power infrastructure expands. Built-in cryptography is effective against some false data injection (FDI) attacks, man-in-the-middle attacks, and tampered data from unauthenticated sources but cannot detect denial of service (DoS) attacks or FDI attacks originating from already-authenticated devices. This paper proposes a Dual-Tier Cyberattack Detection (DTCD) algorithm implemented within a DER aggregator that detects cyberattacks within the cyber and physical layers of a DER-integrated distribution system. The first tier, or cyber filter (CF), applies rule-based cyber checks to detect protocol-level DoS attacks, including TCP floods, SYN floods, and port scan attacks, and timestamp-based FDI anomalies. The second tier, or voltage anomaly detector (VAD), applies a physics-based Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) dual-fusion model to detect event-driven FDI attacks by evaluating whether observed bus voltage deviations can be explained by expected load or photovoltaic (PV) changes. The algorithm is validated in real-time hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing on the PNNL powerNET cyberphysical testbed using an IEEE 123 bus model with DNP3 communication. CF detects all four tested attack signatures under partially mitigated traffic conditions with sub-50 ms detection times. VAD achieves a pooled F1-score of 0.875 and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC) of 0.802 across six attack scenarios at three operating conditions and four test days. VAD completes analysis in 2363 ms on average, within the sub-SCADA timeline. A two-tier comparison study shows that DTCD’s cyber check and physics-based tiers outperform cryptographic and signature-based intrusion detection approaches in the first tier and a standalone-GBM approach in the second tier. The two tiers operate in parallel and provide complementary coverage of DoS and FDI attacks. Replacing CF misses timestamp anomalies, and replacing VAD lowers the FDI F1-score. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively complements cryptographic prevention as a detection layer, can provide cybersecurity coverage for legacy devices through aggregator-level packet screening, and completes its analysis within the sub-SCADA operational window.

title: INSTITUTIONAL, INTERPERSONAL, AND ALGORITHMIC TRUST IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITALIZATION: IMPACT ON THE CREATIVE ECONOMY OF KAZAKHSTAN
abstract: The article examines the phenomenon of hybrid trust in the context of Kazakhstan’s digitalization and its implications for the development of the creative economy. The study addresses institutional, interpersonal, and algorithmic dimensions of trust emerging in citizens’ interactions with e-government, digital services, and artificial intelligence systems. The methodological framework combines the analysis of international indices and surveys (OECD, UNESCO, KPMG, Freedom House, World Values Survey) with original empirical material, including expert in-depth interviews, experimental interviews with chatbots, and case analysis of digital fraud in Kazakhstan in 2024–2025. The findings indicate a discrepancy between the widespread use of digital services and more restrained levels of institutional and algorithmic trust. The analysis suggests that trust in the digital environment can be understood as the outcome of interaction among institutional, interpersonal, and algorithmic factors. In this study, hybrid trust is understood as a specific type of trust emerging from social interaction that is simultaneously mediated by institutions, digital platforms, and algorithms. This form of trust characterizes the user's attitude toward the entire "human–digital intermediary–state institution" interaction chain. The proposed concept of trust is significant for analyzing contemporary digital society.

title: Sustainability intelligence: Integrating Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things, and Digital Twins for resource-efficient and climate-resilient systems
abstract: Sustainability has become one of the defining scientific and societal challenges of the twenty-first century. Climate change, rapid urbanization, population growth, increasing energy demand, and declining natural resources require decision-making that is continuous, adaptive, and supported by reliable environmental intelligence. Conventional monitoring systems, which often rely on periodic measurements and isolated analytical tools, are no longer sufficient for managing highly dynamic environmental systems. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and Digital Twins provide unprecedented opportunities to transform sustainability management from reactive monitoring into intelligent, predictive, and autonomous decision-making. IoT enables continuous environmental sensing, AI extracts knowledge from large heterogeneous datasets, edge intelligence supports low-latency analytics, while Digital Twins create dynamic virtual representations of physical systems capable of simulation and optimization. This critical integrative review examines recent developments in AI-enabled sustainability across smart energy systems, intelligent water management, precision agriculture, transportation, smart buildings, circular economy, and climate resilience. Rather than reviewing these technologies independently, the paper analyzes their interactions within an integrated digital ecosystem and discusses emerging topics including Green AI, carbon-aware computing, explainable AI, federated learning, cybersecurity, and sustainability governance. The review method combines a structured multi-database search with targeted evidence and standards updates through June 2026. Building upon the reviewed literature, the paper introduces the Sustainability Intelligence Framework (SIF), a conceptual seven-layer architecture integrating IoT sensing, edge intelligence, AI analytics, Digital Twins, decision intelligence, and sustainability assessment within a continuous feedback cycle. The proposed framework provides a systems-level perspective for designing adaptive, resilient, and resource-efficient infrastructures capable of supporting future sustainable development. The synthesis identifies continuous, auditable sustainability assessment (Layer 7), rather than the underlying six-layer IoT/cyber–physical stack, as the framework’s distinct contribution. It also shows that reported benefits remain difficult to compare because field validation, system boundaries, rebound effects, and lifecycle digital burdens are inconsistently reported.

title: Energy assistant for buildings: A knowledge-augmented multi-agent framework for market-integrated and occupant-centric energy management
abstract: The growing complexity of modern buildings integrating distributed energy resources such as photovoltaic systems (PV), battery energy storage systems (BESS), electric vehicle (EV) charging stations, heat pumps (HPs) and smart appliances require more intelligent and coordinated energy management strategies. In this context, building-level assistants capable of jointly managing energy assets, occupant comfort and electricity market participation remain largely underexplored. This paper proposes an Energy Assistant for Buildings (EAB) acting as a micro-aggregator based on a hierarchical edge-to-fog architecture that coordinates room-level control, building-level optimization and electricity market interaction. Unlike conventional building energy management systems that typically optimize assets in isolation, rely on fixed supervisory rules or require computationally intensive reinforcement-learning training, the proposed EAB integrates deterministic optimization with knowledge-augmented multi-agent reasoning to coordinate building flexibility, occupant comfort and market participation within a single feasible and safety-constrained decision framework. The Optimizer computes feasible operational schedules and baseline trading strategies, while the Trader and Controller refine these decisions using contextual knowledge and feedback-informed reasoning. Simulation results for an office building equipped with PV, BESS, EV charging and flexible loads demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework. Over a 90-day interval, the framework achieves a Grid Dependence Index (GDI) of 27%, Self-Sufficiency Index (SSI) of 73%, Self-Consumption Index (SCI) of 89%, reducing electricity costs by 84%. Thus, combining hierarchical optimization with knowledge-guided agentic reasoning improves energy autonomy, market responsiveness and economic performance of smart buildings.

title: INTEGRATING RENEWABLE ENERGY AND SMART GRID SYSTEMS: A PATHWAY TO CARBON-NEUTRAL COMMUNITIES IN SOUTHEAST ASIA
venue: International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Literature
abstract: The transition toward carbon-neutral communities has become a global priority, especially in Southeast Asia, where rapid economic growth continues to intensify energy use and carbon emissions. Although the region has substantial renewable energy potential, it remains highly dependent on fossil fuels due to weak grid infrastructure, limited digitalization, and inconsistent policy support. This study systematically synthesizes recent scientific research on the role of smart grid technologies and renewable energy integration in supporting the development of carbon-neutral communities. Using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by PRISMA, 24 peer-reviewed Scopus articles published between 2017 and 2023 were analyzed. The selected literature met predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria and focused on renewable energy adoption, smart grid deployment, and low-carbon community initiatives. The review identifies five major theoretical foundations frequently used in contemporary research: Energy Transition Theory, Smart Grid Theory, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, Resilience Theory, and Socio-Technical Systems Theory. Evidence consistently shows that smart grids powered by IoT, digital automation, advanced metering, and sensor technologies enhance energy efficiency, load management, grid stability, and the integration of renewable sources. The analysis further highlights that socio technical conditions, innovation characteristics, digital readiness, policy frameworks, and community participation significantly shape the adoption of renewable technologies. However, empirical studies remain unevenly distributed, with limited research focusing specifically on rural or tourism-based communities in Southeast Asia. To address these gaps, this study proposes a comprehensive conceptual model that integrates renewable energy, smart grid systems, and socio-technical enablers to support the advancement of carbon-neutral communities.

title: IoT-Enabled Demand Response Framework for Cost-Efficient Smart Energy Systems
venue: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
abstract: The rapid growth of smart grids, Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, and distributed energy resources has transformed traditional power systems into intelligent and interconnected energy ecosystems. Demand Response (DR) programs have emerged as an effective solution for balancing electricity demand and supply while reducing operational costs and improving grid reliability. However, conventional demand response mechanisms often face challenges related to limited real-time monitoring, inefficient load management, delayed decision-making, and insufficient consumer participation. To address these limitations, this research proposes an IoT-Enabled Demand Response Framework for Cost-Efficient Smart Energy Systems (IDRF-CSES). The framework integrates IoT-based energy monitoring, real-time demand forecasting, intelligent load scheduling, adaptive consumer engagement, and cost optimization mechanisms to improve energy efficiency and grid performance. The proposed framework utilizes smart meters, IoT sensors, cloud-based analytics, and machine learning algorithms to continuously monitor energy consumption patterns and dynamically adjust electricity demand according to pricing signals and grid conditions. title: Intelligent Energy Resource Coordination Using Connected Smart Management Devices
venue: International Journal on Advanced Computer Engineering and Communication Technology
abstract: The rapid growth of smart grids, renewable energy systems, distributed energy resources, and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled energy infrastructures has transformed the modern energy management landscape. Efficient coordination of energy resources has become a critical challenge due to the increasing complexity of energy generation, storage, distribution, and consumption processes. Traditional energy management systems often suffer from limited adaptability, delayed decision-making, inefficient resource allocation, and inadequate integration of renewable energy sources. These limitations lead to energy wastage, operational inefficiencies, and reduced grid reliability. Recent advancements in connected smart management devices, intelligent sensing technologies, artificial intelligence, and real-time communication networks provide new opportunities for adaptive energy coordination and optimization. This research proposes an Intelligent Energy Resource Coordination Using Connected Smart Management Devices (IERC-CSMD) framework that integrates smart sensors, connected management devices, intelligent monitoring systems, machine learning-based optimization, dynamic resource allocation, and real-time energy control mechanisms. The proposed framework continuously monitors energy demand, generation capacity, storage availability, and network conditions to coordinate energy resources efficiently.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Energy Management: Investigate How Al and Machine Learning Algorithms Can Optimize Energy Consumption, Improve Efficiency, and Reduce Costs in Various Electrical Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning offer tremendous potential to transform energy management across buildings, renewable sources, and electrical grid infrastructure. This paper provides a comprehensive review of relevant AI techniques and applications for optimizing energy usage, increasing efficiency, and reducing costs. Proposed AI methods include neural networks for predictive analytics, reinforcement learning for adaptive control systems, and computer vision for monitoring and fault detection. AI-based solutions for automated energy management range from smart thermostats in homes to AI agents coordinating decentralize distribution on smart grids. However, issues around explainability, security, and data quality must be addressed. If AI continues rapid advancement, further intelligent energy breakthroughs could emerge to cut consumption, maximize renewables, and bring the electrical grid into the 21st century.

title: Mitigating Cyber Risks in Smart Cyber-Physical Power Systems Through Deep Learning and Hybrid Security Models
venue: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
abstract: The increasing integration of smart cyber physical power systems with communication networks has increased exposure to cyber threats, requiring advanced intrusion detection solutions. This work presents a deep learning based framework using the Cybersecurity Intrusion Simulated Network dataset and PSCAD generated cyber threat scenarios. Data preprocessing includes standardization, categorical encoding, and SMOTEENN sampling. Multiple models, namely Convolutional Neural Network, Long Short Term Memory, Transformer, and a hybrid CNN LSTM architecture, are trained with hyperparameter optimization. Experimental evaluation shows that the CNN LSTM hybrid achieves the highest performance, reaching 95.3% accuracy and 94.4% F1 score on the Cyber Threat dataset, and 99.9% accuracy with 99.9% F1 score on PSCAD simulations. Explainable AI techniques, including LIME and SHAP, are integrated to interpret feature contributions and enhance trust. For practical deployment, the optimized model is implemented using a Flask based web application enabling real time monitoring. The system classifies grid traffic into no attack, attack detected, injection attack, MITM, replay attack, and spoofing attack categories. The proposed approach delivers accurate, interpretable, and scalable intrusion detection for resilient smart grid cybersecurity operations worldwide deployments.

title: Semi-Supervised Learning under Inductive, Fairness and Privacy Constraints
venue: Institutional Research Information System University of Turin (University of Turin)
abstract: This thesis investigates semi-supervised learning (SSL) methodologies under inductive, fairness, and privacy constraints.In a supervised learning setting, every instance is labeled (i.e. it has the target variable).In a semisupervised learning setting, there are both labeled and unlabeled instances.In order to make a prediction, SSL algorithms leverage the observed mapping between features and labels of labeled instances, and the distribution of features of unlabeled ones.There are two main families of SSL algorithms: transductive and inductive.In the first part of this thesis, we propose a SSL framework to make inductive any transductive method.The typical SSL setting, where there is a scarcity of labels, could lead to the amplification of biases already present in the data: any machine learning algorithm should avoid biases present in historical data and this task is even more challenging when there is only a small number of labeled instances.For this reason, in the second part of this thesis, we investigate a debiasing training method to provide fair representations in a SSL setting.Lastly, in the final part of this manuscript, we study a particular setting of SSL where the labeled instances have privacy constraints.We build up on the definition of differential privacy and conduct different experiments to prove the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Gemelos digitales habilitados por inteligencia artificial en sistemas eléctricos y energéticos: revisión sistemática de aplicaciones, arquitecturas, validación y tendencias emergentes
abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) se integra cada vez más con los gemelos digitales (DT) para mejorar el monitoreo, la predicción, el diagnóstico, la optimización y el control de sistemas eléctricos y energéticos. Esta revisión sistemática analiza aplicaciones de DT habilitados por IA publicadas entre 2020 y 2025, considerando dominios de aplicación, técnicas de IA, fuentes de datos, estrategias de validación, niveles de madurez, desafíos y tendencias emergentes. Se analizó un corpus de 56 documentos, de los cuales 24 estudios aplicados conformaron el núcleo técnico. El Deep Learning fue la familia de IA más utilizada (41,7%), seguida del Machine Learning convencional (25,0%) y el Reinforcement Learning (16,7%). Las redes eléctricas y sistemas multi-energía, junto con las energías renovables, fueron los dominios más representados, cada uno con el 25,0%. Además, el 83,3% de los estudios utilizó datos reales o híbridos y el 75,0% se clasificó como Intelligent Digital Twin. Los principales desafíos se relacionan con ciberseguridad, escalabilidad computacional, operación en tiempo real, calidad de datos, interoperabilidad y validación en entornos operacionales.

title: Artificial Intelligence Supporting Sustainable Energy Management: A Comparative Case Study of European Projects
abstract: Purpose: The aim of this article is to comparatively analyse the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in selected European projects related to energy management and to develop an analytical framework for classifying AI applications according to their functions, the types of data used, associated technologies and digital components, and the level of AI application. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study employed a qualitative comparative case study analysis of three European research and innovation projects: DATAWiSE, BD4NRG, and TwinEU. The analysis was based on publicly available secondary data, primarily project documentation and institutional sources.Findings: The analysis identified three distinct configurations of AI application.DATAWiSE represents AI application at the building level, BD4NRG at the level of services and the energy data ecosystem, and TwinEU at the level of energy system infrastructure.The projects differ in terms of AI functions, the types of data used, and associated digital technologies.The results show that similar AI functions may occur in different management and technological contexts and should therefore be considered within the broader data and technological environment. Practical Implications: The proposed framework may support the systematic comparison of AI applications in energy-related projects by identifying relationships between AI functions, the data environment, associated digital technologies, and the level of application. It may also provide a structured basis for analysing further European energy projects. Originality/Value:The study proposes a multidimensional analytical framework combining AI functions, the type of data used, associated technologies and digital components, and the level of AI application.It also distinguishes between the use of AI in sustainable energy management processes and the demonstrated sustainability outcomes of its application.Given the exploratory nature of the study, the framework is intended to organise and compare the analysed cases rather than provide a universal typology of AI applications in the energy sector.

title: Integrating energy pricing and green technology in residential building management: a panel threshold analysis for sustainable construction in China
abstract: Urban residential buildings account for a growing share of China’s electricity consumption, yet strategies for integrating energy-efficient technologies with price-responsive building design remain underdeveloped. This study examines threshold effects of technological innovation (input intensity [R&D] and green patents [GP]) on household electricity consumption (HEC) using data from 30 Chinese provinces (2005-2020). Two-way fixed-effects and panel threshold regression models are employed. Results show that R&D exhibits a single threshold at 0.40%, while GP presents dual thresholds at 456 and 1567 units. Across regimes, electricity price (EP) responsiveness declines, with elasticity reductions of 26.3% under the GP model and 22.5% under the R&D model. Heterogeneity analysis reveals regional and socioeconomic differences: eastern region has higher price elasticity (-1.187) than central and western regions, while high-income households show 52% stronger price responsiveness (-2.028) than low-income groups (-1.330). This study contributes in three ways: (1) identifying nonlinear changes in HEC price elasticity across innovation regimes; (2) revealing R&D and GP thresholds that reshape price responsiveness; and (3) demonstrating heterogeneity in price elasticity across regions, urbanization levels and income groups. The findings provide guidance for urban residential buildings and policy design in China.

title: Analisis Deviasi Pengukuran Energi Listrik antara kWh Meter PLN dan Power Meter Digital pada Site BTS Telekomunikasi
venue: JASEE Journal of Application and Science on Electrical Engineering
abstract: A base transceiver station site operates continuously, so electricity cost is a major operationalexpenditure. Two energy meters normally work in parallel at such a site: the utility kilowatt-hourmeter used as the legal basis for billing and an internal digital power meter connected to the powermanagement system for operational monitoring. A discrepancy between the two readings canreduce the reliability of bill verification. This study analyses the measurement deviation betweenboth instruments at a base transceiver station site in Lamongan Regency and evaluates the voltageprofile, current profile, and three-phase load unbalance at the same site. A comparative quantitativemethod was applied by recording both meters at four observation points within ten days. Duringthe ten-day period, the utility meter registered 2216.08 kilowatt-hours, while the digital powermeter registered 2205.35 kilowatt-hours, giving a deviation of 10.73 kilowatt-hours or 0.48 percent.This value is lower than the ±1 percent class 1 benchmark used for comparison in this study. Thevoltage unbalance stayed below two percent, whereas the current unbalance reached 29 to 46percent; therefore, redistribution of the single-phase loads is recommended.

title: Makine öğrenenimi kullanılarak talep cevabına dayalı dinamik fiyatlandırma
abstract: Bu araştırmada amaç, dinamik fiyatlandırma için derin öğrenme yaklaşımını kullanarak arz tarafı yönetim sisteminin performansını veri belirsizliği karşısında incelenmesidir. Pekiştirme aracı olarak aktör-eleştirmen aracı yöntemini kullanılarak, hem enerji talebi hem de fiyatlara ilişkin yüksek düzeyde tahmine dayalı veriler elde edilerek, enerji tüketimi kalıplarının ve fiyat dalgalanmalarının kapsamlı bir şekilde anlaşılması kolaylaştırıldı. Önerilen takviye öğrenmeye dayalı dinamik fiyatlandırma yaklaşımı, iki tahmin senaryosu aracılığıyla değerlendirilmiştir: gerçek ve öngörülen talebin karşılaştırılması ve gerçek ve öngörülen fiyatların karşılaştırılması. İlk olarak, temel tahminler için uzun kısa süreli hafıza (LSTM) modeli kullanıldı. Daha sonra tahminleri iyileştirmek için derin RL modeli uygulandı ve dikkate değer iyileştirmeler sağlandı. Derin RL modelinin 30 dakikalık aralıklarla fiyat tahminlerinde %99'luk kayda değer bir doğruluk oranına ulaşması dikkat çekicidir. Bulgular, önerilen modelin hem talebi hem de fiyatı doğru bir şekilde tahmin etmedeki etkinliğini ve dolayısıyla enerji yönetimi amaçlarına uygunluğunu kesin olarak göstermektedir.

abstract: Bu tez, enerji üretimindeki temel yapay zeka metodolojilerinin en yaygın uygulamalarını araştırmaktadır. title: Predictive Analytics for Demand-Side Management in Sustainable Smart Cities
venue: National Journal of Intelligent Power Systems and Technology
abstract: This is backed by the current state of urbanization that is increasingly being accelerated by the escalating infiltration of the distributed renewable energyglobals, which are creating new complexity in the managing of the distributed modern power systems in smart cities. The traditional theories of demand-side management (DSM) which to date have been fixed-price schemes or reactionary measures can no longer react to the change and variability of energy demands and renewable resources. One of the future frameworks that enables the taking of proactive measures and is made possible by the AI-driven technique of predictive analytics is a promise of the prospective framework, which is driven by machine learning (ML) and big data technology. Real-time data streams (smart meters and IoT-enabled appliances), weather projections, socio-economic data, and time-dependent energy consumption can be used to provide predictions therefore enabling the optimization of renewable integration and dynamic consumer engagement with the help of adaptable price formation. The role of predictive analytics in terms of accelerating DSS models in the context of sustainable smart cities has been discussed in the present paper with a focus on such methods as short-term load predictions using deep learning frameworks, hybrid renewable generation prediction and forecasting models, consumer analytics, and demand response optimization using reinforcement learning. Future smart city scenario demonstration through a testbed demonstrates the actual benefits of predictive DSM with a reduction in peak demands down to 25 percent, 30 percent more renewable use through minimized curtailment, and a possible 15 percent cut in household energy expenses through dynamical tariffs. The results also indicate that predictive analytics have the potential to enhance grid reliability and resilience and attain user buy-in through the definition of personalized approaches to the demand response based on the behavior tendency. Despite these odds, such as data privacy, complex computations, and operation on a heterogeneous infrastructure, the hubbub of predictive analytics as a key fulcrum to actualize the vision of sustainable, resilient and consumer-driven energy management in next generation smart cities is not taking a holiday.

title: 5G-Enabled Real-Time Monitoring Framework for Cyber-Physical Power Systems
venue: National Journal of Intelligent Power Systems and Technology
abstract: The renewable energy integration, distributed generation, and intelligent automation of power grids have turned them into complex cyber-physical power systems (CPPS) with the nature of coherent interplay between physical and cyber layers being key to their stability, resilience, and sustainability. CPPS needs real-time monitoring and control, which is not able to be adequately provided with the current LTE or Wi-Fi. To overcome this issue, this paper suggests a 5G-based real-time monitoring system, which combines advanced sensory devices, a strong communication infrastructure, edge computing, and anomaly detection with artificial intelligence (AI). Phasor measurement units (PMUs), intelligent electronic devices (IEDs), and IoT sensors are used to obtain wide-area situational awareness and 5G ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) slices to provide a deterministic delivery of mission-critical data. Hybrid AI systems such as CNN-LSTM networks that run on edge nodes can detect anomalies and predictive maintenance almost instantly with minimal dependence on centralized clouds. Co-simulation of the 5G New Radio (NR) networks and the IEEE 118-bus test system is used to validate the framework in NS-3. It has results which show sub-millisecond response times, a rate of greater than 99.9 percent packet delivery, three times higher throughput than LTE, and an error reporting accuracy of more than 97 percent. Moreover, the inclusion of blockchains improves cybersecurity by preventing attacks of false data injection. The suggested system creates a reliable and scalable architecture of autonomous energy systems in 6G in the future.

title: Data Privacy in the Cloud: Trends, Risks, and Organizational Practices
venue: MBSTU Journal of science and technology
abstract: Cloud computing is increasingly leveraged by Bangladeshi organizations, including utilities, financial institutions, and technology firms, for scalable data storage and analytic capabilities. However, migrating sensitive operational and personal data to cloud environments introduces serious privacy challenges. This study investigates the evolving trends, risks, and organizational practices related to data privacy in the cloud within the Bangladeshi context. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 132 IT and security decision-makers such as CISOs, cloud architects, and compliance officers to assess perceived risks, governance maturity, and technical control adoption. Key findings reveal that misconfiguration, insider threat, and weak key management are viewed as the most significant risks, while regulatory compliance (e.g., under Bangladesh’s new Personal Data Protection Ordinance) is also a major concern. On the governance front, 70% of organizations report having a formal data-governance framework, with over half using shared-responsibility matrices and including audit and breach-notification clauses in contracts. Technically, encryption (at-rest and in-transit) is widely used, but only a small fraction of firms has adopted advanced privacy-preserving technologies, such as homomorphic encryption or TEEs. Trust in cloud service providers is moderate (mean score ~3.6/5) and correlates strongly with governance maturity and external audits. Based on these insights and the regulatory landscape in Bangladesh, we organize organizational cloud privacy practices into a five-phase risk-management framework (Assessment, Design, Implementation, Monitoring, Review) to help organizations enhance their cloud privacy posture which is grounded theory in institutional and IT governance logic.

title: A Strategic Roadmap and Policy Framework for Smart Grid Transition in Uganda
abstract: Uganda’s installed electricity generation capacity has expanded, yet persistent distribution losses, ageing assets, limited feeder level visibility and emerging requirements for prosumer participation continue to constrain reliable electricity delivery. This study develops a Uganda specific strategic roadmap and policy framework for smart grid transition. It applies a structured review and synthesis of academic, legal, regulatory, utility and development-sector evidence to assess Uganda’s institutional and technical readiness. The findings show that Uganda’s immediate priority is not system-wide deployment of advanced digital technologies, but clear institutional responsibilities, verified feeder baselines, common technical requirements and targeted pilots. The proposed roadmap comprises four overlapping phases: regulatory and institutional foundations; distribution visibility and pilot validation; system integration and performance-based expansion; and advanced control and regional coordination. Progression between phases is tied to demonstrated improvements in distribution losses, reliability, voltage performance, data quality and whole life value rather than equipment installation alone. The study further defines a feeder-prioritisation method, institutional roles, readiness conditions and mitigation measures for financing, procurement, cybersecurity, interoperability, workforce capacity, regulation, data quality and coordination. The resulting framework provides a practical basis for directing investment and regulation towards measurable network improvements that support industrialisation, distributed energy resources and a more reliable and flexible Ugandan power system.

title: Next-Generation Intelligent Power Systems: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization and Blockchain-Enabled Cybersecurity for Secure Energy Infrastructures
venue: National Journal of Intelligent Power Systems and Technology
abstract: Modern power systems are growingly complex due to the mass adoption of renewable energy, electrification of the transport sector, and digitalization, which require infrastructures that, alongside being energy-efficient, must be secure, adaptive, and resilient. This article introduces a unified framework that merges machine learning (ML) led optimization with blockchain-based cybersecurity to further the achievements of the applications of the next generation intelligent power systems. The ML module deep learning algorithm and reinforcement learning are used to do proper forecasting of the loads, optimal scheduling of renewable energy systems as well as identify anomalies with short lead-time, thus contributing to increased operational efficiency. Simultaneously, the block chain layer provides a decentralized and tamper-proof means of achieving secure transaction in energy, logging of operation activities and peer-2-peer (P2P) energy trading. Increased resolution, real-time streams of data are available using IoT/enabled sensing devices, and demand response and trading mechanisms are automatically enforced through smart contracts. The simulation research carried out by both MATLAB Simulink and Hyperledger Fabric shows that it increases energy efficiency by 21%, peak load demand by 17%, fault detection accuracy by 14.8%, and transactions latency down by 35 percent. The findings confirm the suggested architecture as a scaleable route to AI-optimized and cyber-protected power infrastructure systems with the potential to support high renewable penetration but which are both trusted and reliable in dynamic energy systems and adaptable to new market and socio-economic realities.

title: Z-mOPE: a unified model for secure multi-dimensional indexing and query processing via order-preserving encoding
abstract: Efficient query processing over encrypted multi-dimensional data remains challenging due to the inherent trade-off between confidentiality, query expressiveness, and computational efficiency. Existing order-preserving encryption (OPE) schemes support efficient query execution but are primarily designed for one-dimensional domains, whereas stronger cryptographic approaches often incur prohibitive computational overhead. This paper presents Z-mOPE, a unified model for secure multi-dimensional indexing and query processing that extends mutable order-preserving encoding by integrating Z-order space-filling mapping with an OPE-enhanced B + -tree index. The proposed model enables a broad spectrum of encrypted multi-dimensional queries (including point, range, k nearest neighbour, constrained k nearest neighbour, and skyline queries) to be evaluated directly over ciphertexts while preserving the IND-OCPA ideal-security guarantees and maintaining logarithmic index operations. The paper introduces client-server protocols for all supported queries, establishes correctness, and provides rigorous asymptotic analyses of index construction and query processing. Extensive experiments on real-life and synthetic datasets demonstrate that Z-mOPE, together with its complementary Hilbert curve-based variant, preserves the I/O behaviour of the corresponding plaintext index while incurring additional computational and communication overhead associated with confidentiality-preserving query processing, and consistently outperforms representative encrypted query processing schemes in scalability, query expressiveness, and practical applicability. These results establish Z-mOPE as a practically deployable model that bridges strong confidentiality, expressive query processing, and efficient management of dynamic multi-dimensional data.

title: Impact of IoT-Based Energy Management Systems on Energy Use in Urban Commercial Buildings
venue: Journal of Educational Innovation and Research
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies into energy management systems has garnered significant attention due to its potential to optimize energy usage in urban environments. Despite the growing adoption of IoT in building management, there remains a lack of experimental research that rigorously tests the causal impact of IoT-based systems on energy consumption in real-world settings. This study aims to fill this gap by experimentally evaluating the effect of IoT-based energy management systems on energy efficiency in urban commercial buildings. An experimental study was conducted involving [N] urban commercial buildings, with [N1] assigned to the experimental group and [N2] to the control group, over a period of [X] months. Our experimental design uniquely combines controlled conditions and real-time data monitoring to assess the causal relationship between IoT system implementation and energy savings. We conducted an experimental study with both an experimental group, exposed to the IoT-based system, and a control group. The results showed a significant reduction in energy consumption in the experimental group, confirming the hypothesis that IoT systems can improve energy efficiency. The experimental design allowed for a precise isolation of the effects of IoT, ensuring the validity of the findings. These findings not only advance our understanding of the impact of IoT on energy consumption but also provide practical insights for the implementation of smart energy management systems in various sectors. The results are relevant for policymakers and building managers, offering evidence-based guidance for adopting IoT technologies to optimize energy usage in urban infrastructure.

title: A NOVEL FRAMEWORK FOR SMART BUILDING APPLICATIONS IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF VACANT SPACE
venue: Journal of Intelligent Machine Learning and IoT Enabled Applications
abstract: The intelligent use of building spaces is one of the main demands of the intelligent infrastructure of the present time. The quick advancements in the sphere of smart building technologies and Internet of Things (IoT) systems have allowed constant monitoring of indoor areas, but the correct identification of empty and occupied areas remains a rather problematic issue because of dynamic human behavior and uncertainties in sensors and uneven information sources. The present paper suggests a new paradigm of the smart building application that would help to correctly identify the vacant spaces based on smart data-driven methodology. The framework unites the information gathered through the distributed sensors including motion, occupancy, environmental, and energy usage sensors, with the state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms to examine the real-time and historical trends in space use. Powerful preprocessing and feature extraction algorithms are used to deal with noise, missing, and time variations. The main goal of the suggested framework is to facilitate the quality and reliable detection of the vacant space besides being scalable and energy efficient. Experimental assessments indicate that the framework is efficient in estimating vacant spaces to a high level of accuracy, allowing to optimize the allocation of resources, energy conservation, and comfort of occupants. The suggested solution offers an effective and sensible solution to smart buildings management and sustainable development of infrastructure.

title: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies in Knowledge Engineering for Sensitive Data Applications in AI-Enabled Intelligent Engineering Systems
venue: CPS Digital Library - Series of Conferences
abstract: The proliferation of artificial intelligence in intelligent engineering systems has created a highly connected network physical system, which can optimize itself and make real-time decisions. The knowledge engineering pipeline for constructing digital twins, fault diagnosis ontology and adaptive process model usually deals with sensitive data, company data and personal data. This review discusses privacy protection technologies: differential privacy, federated learning, homomorphic encryption and secure multi-party computing. They are an important part of knowledge engineering and can protect the privacy of intelligent engineering systems driven by artificial intelligence. This analysis uses the life cycle principle in system engineering, the feedback theory of network physical system, and the information theory formula about the trade-off between privacy and practicality. Specific integration is evaluated, including digital twins for continuous synchronization, reinforcement learning for dynamic planning, computer vision for online fault detection, and edge computing for deterministic control, and the deployment in real life is considered. The application of intelligent manufacturing, medical care network physical system and intelligent transportation shows great progress in collective intelligence and work efficiency, but there are still problems such as precision loss, long calculation time and security loopholes. Our new idea is to use a control method to treat privacy noise as a minor problem, and to create a system that uses reinforcement learning to select the best method to protect data. We believe that to use these technologies confidently, we need to protect the standard rules and models of privacy from the beginning, and improve the current standards of digital twins and systems engineering.

title: SMART IRRIGATION USING TRANSFER LEARNING IN IOT-BASED AGRICULTURAL NETWORKS
venue: Journal of Intelligent Machine Learning and IoT Enabled Applications
abstract: The management of water in agriculture is an important issue in contemporary agriculture, as the lack of water is growing, climatic changes are becoming apparent, and the volume of food production is increasing. The old method of irrigation usually is based on the fixed period or manual regulation resulting in the waste of water and the low optimization of crop production. To overcome these drawbacks, the present paper will suggest a transfer learningbased smart irrigation system to optimize the management of water in agricultural IoT-based networks. The suggested system incorporates distributed IoT sensors to monitor soil moisture, temperature, and humidity, among other environmental conditions continuously, and uses transfer learning to adapt the pre-trained deep learning models in order to make precise irrigation decisions with little agricultural data. Sensor data will be sent to a centralized platform where smart models are applied to compute the water needs of the crops and in real time dynamically turn the irrigation actuators. The experimental findings indicate that the proposed system has a great positive effect on the accuracy of irrigation and the amount of water used and the overall health of crops in comparison to the traditional methods of irrigation. Transfer learning combined with IoT allows converging models more quickly, more accurately, and scale to a wide range of agricultural scenarios, so the system becomes a viable and sustainable remedy to the precision agriculture and smart farming application.

title: Design and Evaluation of Energy Storage–Supported Renewable Microgrids for Reliable and Resilient Power Supply
venue: National Journal of Renewable Energy Systems and Innovation
abstract: The fast adoption of renewable energy by modern power systems has added pressure to the complexity of implementing powerful micro grid systems that can provide consistent, robust, and sustainable power. Renewable energy sources like solar photovoltaic and wind energies are environmentally friendly but have natural intermittency and uncertainty problems that may affect power system stability, and continuity. The given paper introduces an in-depth design and assessment package of the energy storage-facilitated renewable microgrids that will help to increase the performance consistency and operational sustainability of the system. The suggested microgrid system incorporates solar PV and wind energy production with a hybrid energy storage system that consists of lithium-ion batteries, supercapacitors, and allows energy balancing over a long time and mitigation response to transient events. A smart energy management approach is created where the optimal synchronisation of the renewable generation, storage dispatch and load demand under the grid-connected operating and the islanded operating modes are planned without overlooking the important loads in times of disturbance. The effectiveness of the suggested framework is analysed with the help of specific simulation experiments based on the realistic profile of renewable generation and demand. The main performance indices such as reliability indices, energy not supplied, voltage and frequency stability, disturbance recovery time and storage utilisation efficiency are systematically analysed. The findings indicate that hybrid energy storage as an addition to the microgrids can greatly enhance the reliability of the microgrids, minimise power outages, boost the use of renewable energy, and expedite the recovery rates after faults than storage-only systems. In addition, the synchronized working show of the battery and supercapacitor systems reduces stress in storage and enhances efficiency of the systems in use. The microgrid framework proposed with the help of energy storage will offer a robust and scalable approach to a reliable power supply in critical infrastructure, remote communities, and resilience-oriented energy frameworks.

Blockchain can be effectively combined with AI in the work of smart grids with its decentralized immutable traceability and ability to forecast, suggest, and identify anomalies, and with data security, transparency, and integrity, on another level, making smart grids capable of functioning autonomously and efficiently. The feasibility of integrating AI and Blockchain to optimise smart grids on a platform of IoT with the view of employing them in the real-time management of energy is discussed in the paper. A conceptual scheme of the way these technologies could be applied in smart grid systems is proposed, and after it, the discussion of the potential use of these technologies, their challenges, and solutions is presented. Based on the study, smart grids that rely on the IoT will be more efficient, secure, and scalable and combining them with the AI and the Blockchain may offer a chance of attaining sustainability in energy management within smart cities.

title: Edge AI-Enabled Smart Energy Meter Using STM32 and IoT for Real-Time Power Theft Detection with TinyML
venue: International Conference on Soft Computing for Security Applications (ICSCSA)
abstract: Smart grid and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have ushered a more intelligent, secure, energy-efficient era of electricity monitoring, which has raised the increasing need to identify power theft as it happens. Cloud-centric solutions often face communication latency, power usage and scalability issues for edge deployment. TinyML for Real-time Power Theft Detection - This paper presents an approach called “TinyML” to detect power theft in real-time using an Edge AI system with smart energy metering using STM32 and IoT. The designed framework integrates different hardware components including an STM32 microcontroller; voltage sensors, current sensors, tamper detection modules, LoRaWAN and Wi-Fi communication, and an IoT cloud platform with TinyML enabled local anomaly detection. The novelty of this work is the ability to implement minimizing cloud dependency and computational impact, while combining Explainable AI (XAI), embedded intelligence in the STM32 SoC, secured communication on the IoT while maintaining low latency for theft detection. Experimental verification shows that the power theft detection accuracy is 98.9%, the energy monitoring accuracy is 99.1%, the Mean Square Error is reduced 31% compared with traditional cloud-based solutions, and the communication latency can be reduced below 180 ms. In addition, the proposed framework can decrease energy consumption and allows for scaling up to next generation smart grids. The system offers reliable real-time monitoring, intelligent decision making, optimized energy management, and cost-effective cyber defense functions in the energy distribution system, both for residential and industrial applications.

title: An Adaptive Sporadic Method for Emergency Telemetry Processing in Distributed Energy Facility Control Systems
abstract: This paper develops an adaptive sporadic method for processing emergency telemetry in automated control systems for distributed energy facilities. The study formalizes the information flow produced by cyclic polling and shows that, under stationary operation, the corresponding telecontrol flow normally does not overload the control center. In emergency conditions, however, near-simultaneous messages generated by several remote terminal units may form a bursty peak flow that increases processing latency and reduces the timeliness of supervisory control. To reduce this load, the paper refines the distribution of functions among the remote terminal unit, the line adapter, the control station controller, and the operator workstation. The proposed method extends conventional sporadic transmission by local event identification, adaptive deadband control for measured variables, duplicate suppression, priority-based emergency queues, event time stamping, and buffer occupancy monitoring. The mathematical model relates packet service time, message arrival intensity, and control center utilization; it also introduces a filtering coefficient that characterizes the reduction of the emergency flow before data reach the control center. The approach is compatible with event-driven reporting and spontaneous transmission mechanisms used in IEC 60870-5-104 and DNP3-based telecontrol systems. The resulting method reduces non-informative traffic and improves the robustness of emergency data acquisition under limited communication bandwidth and finite processing capacity.

title: Impact of Household Characteristics on Residential Power Demand Temperature Sensitivity
venue: IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference
abstract: Residential electricity demand is strongly influenced by outdoor temperature. However, the temperature sensitivity vary substantially across households and are often treated homogeneously in power-system analysis. This paper presents an empirical household-level study of residential temperature sensitivity using real-world, full-year 15-minute smart meter data from 177 residential consumers, combined with matched survey data capturing household characteristics, behaviors, and motivations. Temperature sensitivity is extracted directly from measured electricity consumption and used to classify households into warmsensitive, cold-sensitive, and non-temperature-sensitive groups. Results indicate that temperature sensitivity is widespread yet highly heterogeneous, with cooling-driven sensitivity dominating. Survey analysis shows that temperature sensitivity aligns systematically with housing characteristics, household composition, and motivational attributes, while frequent energy-saving behaviors do not necessarily correspond to reduced temperature-driven electricity demand. Furthermore, temperature-sensitive households report greater willingness to modify electricity-use behavior in response to financial incentives and enabling technologies. By integrating operational smart-meter measurements with surveybased household characterization at the household level, this work provides empirical insights into residential load variability that are not observable from smart meter data alone and supports improved customer segmentation and demand response program design for electric utilities.

title: Planning considerations for smart meter implementations in South Africa
abstract: Smart meter implementations are still in their infancy in many African countries. This is evident by the lack of research on the subject in the African context. Most of the research studies are either Eurocentric or US-centric. Although these studies are important and informative, they might not address the African challenges in context. Hence, South Africa was chosen as the testbed for an investigation that addresses the apparent knowledge gap. This study set out to formulate a framework for planning considerations in the implementation of smart meter technology within South Africa. Through extensive literature review and analysis, the technology acceptance model (TAM) was chosen as a foundational framework for this study. Although TAM is widely used for researching technology acceptance and use, its applicability was found to be inadequate in explaining customer centric factors in smart metering. Therefore, it was supplemented with factors from the theory of reasoned action (TRA), the theory of planned behavior (TPB), privacy calculus theory (PCT), as well as the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT). A total of 11 consumer-centric factors were identified, and these were statistically analysed using the structural equation modelling technique (SEM). Ten (10) consumer-centric factors was found to be significant. These were attitude, perceived value, monetary cost, privacy risk, perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, facilitating conditions, social norms, trust in technology and behavioral intention. Hypothesis testing confirmed that, not one acceptance model could adequately be used to identify and explain the consumer-centric factors that can be incorporated for planning considerations for smart meter implementation in South Africa. It was further observed that the consumer-centric factors such as environmental issues, security, reliability and health issues that were important in developed countries were not deemed so in South Africa. From a methodological perspective, the study attests to contextual localised application as opposed to universal meaning and measurement invariance when incorporating planning consideration for smart meter implementation in South Africa as compared to European countries and the United States of America. Finally, the findings hold some practical implications, as they showed the practical utility of the model in predicting the consumer-centric factors that can be incorporated for planning considerations. In support, the Business Model Canvas (BMC) was found to be a useful tool in deriving and reporting on the formulation of planning consideration guidelines. Using the BMC, five planning consideration guidelines were derived: customer segmentation, partnerships, benefits communication, value identification and customer attitude. These planning considerations will allow smart meter providers to identify their customers, partners and value propositions they might need to offer consumers to facilitate a higher smart meter acceptance and use. The proposed planning consideration guidelines can practically be used by policymakers and regulators for several aspects for future pervasive technology acceptance studies. This research has, therefore, created a platform for further research in the smart technology domain while providing a usable predictive framework for the identification of consumer-centric factors and formulation of planning considerations guidelines for smart meter implementation within the South African context.

title: System‐Aware Model Compression for Real‐Time Intelligent Monitoring in Edge Power IoT
abstract: ABSTRACT Real‐time intelligent monitoring in modern power Internet of things (power IoT) systems faces severe challenges due to edge resource constraints and unpredictable runtime behaviour. Existing compression methods often ignore practical system‐level metrics, leading to suboptimal deployment. This paper proposes a unified system‐aware model compression framework for edge power IoT environments. Rather than treating compression as an isolated algorithmic task, we incorporate deployment architecture, edge runtime constraints and lifecycle management into the design. The framework integrates layer‐wise controllable pruning, deployment‐oriented quantisation and compression–distillation co‐design into a single workflow targeting deployable artefacts under realistic conditions. Extensive experiments on ARM‐ and AMD64‐based platforms show the approach achieves up to reduction in model size and significant latency improvements, including tighter tail latency under containerised CPU execution. The co‐design effectively recovers accuracy lost to aggressive compression without adding inference‐time overhead. Beyond inference, measured loading results and a simulation‐based distribution analysis indicate substantial reductions in lifecycle overhead and update failure rates. These results confirm that system‐aware co‐design is essential for enabling reliable, scalable and real‐time intelligent monitoring in edge power IoT systems.

title: Safe machine learning–based active network control for renewable dominated distribution systems: A UK distribution network case study
abstract: Distribution networks are growing more complex and unpredictable because of the high amount of distributed energy resources (DERs), especially solar panels. Traditional machine learning (ML) methods do not provide safety assurances in important situations, while optimization-based approaches offer formal safety guarantees but struggle with scalability and speed in real-time environments. This paper introduces a hybrid supervised learning approach for managing distribution networks in the UK power system using real data in Neplan software combined with python. It combines ML forecasts for energy demand and solar generation with a simplified power flow model and a supervisory safety system that ensures voltage levels stay within legal limits while reducing the need to cut off renewable energy. ML handles routine decisions, while a quadratic safety layer steps in only when potential issues are detected, allowing for quick, clear, and compliant operations aligned with RIIO-2 regulations. The approach was tested on a real UK network covering 894 substations using hourly data throughout the year, implemented in Python. The results showed no voltage violations, better control of voltage levels around 1.00 p.u., and a significant drop in solar curtailment, from about 28,000 kW to less than 4,000 kW. This suggests the method has strong potential to support higher renewable energy integration while ensuring network stability in future low-carbon power systems.

title: Tecnologías en electricidad. Revisiones bibliográficas y aplicaciones sostenibles
abstract: Los sistemas eléctricos se encuentran inmersos en una transformación tecnológica que está redefiniendo la manera de generar, distribuir, supervisar, proteger y utilizar la energía. La expansión de las fuentes renovables, la generación distribuida, el almacenamiento energético, las microredes y los dispositivos conectados converge con el desarrollo de sensores, automatización, comunicaciones digitales, analítica de datos e inteligencia artificial, configurando infraestructuras con nuevas capacidades de observación, coordinación y gestión. Sus contenidos recorren los fundamentos necesarios para comprender los fenómenos y componentes eléctricos y avanzan hacia el estudio de las redes modernas, los sistemas de protección, la calidad de la energía, la digitalización, la supervisión, la automatización y la eficiencia energética. Sustentado en literatura científica reciente, el libro examina la evolución de la detección de fallas, la coordinación de protecciones, el diagnóstico de perturbaciones, la observación de redes, la integración de recursos energéticos distribuidos y la gestión inteligente del consumo. A este análisis se incorporan propuestas de desarrollo tecnológico que articulan los conocimientos examinados en arquitecturas susceptibles de posteriores procesos de diseño, implementación y validación. Dirigida a estudiantes, docentes, investigadores y profesionales, la obra trasciende la explicación convencional del funcionamiento de los sistemas eléctricos para ofrecer una comprensión de su evolución y de los desafíos que acompañan su creciente complejidad. En sus páginas, conocimiento técnico, evidencia científica e innovación convergen para interpretar una realidad energética cada vez más distribuida, digitalizada y dinámica, en la que el desafío no consiste únicamente en disponer de electricidad, sino en desarrollar las capacidades necesarias para supervisarla, protegerla, gestionarla y aprovecharla de manera eficiente, segura y sostenible.

title: A Confidentiality-Aware AI-Assisted Digital Workflow Framework for Quality and Efficiency Improvement in Power Utility Operations
venue: Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The renewable-dominated new power system increases enterprise-side coordination, documentation, and traceability requirements in power utilities. In practice, operational workflow governance is often performed through fragmented folders and informal reminders, making document readiness, post-event archiving, and audit tracking difficult to manage. To address this problem while preserving data confidentiality, this paper presents a confidentiality-aware AI-assisted digital workflow framework for power utility operations. Developed from a de-identified real-world application scenario, the framework converts annual operational plans into standardized workspaces, checks document readiness, tracks post-event archiving, and visualizes lifecycle states through an operational governance dashboard. A document readiness and archiving completeness index is introduced together with an operational evidence ledger to quantify workflow quality and provide traceable records. A local or internal AI gateway is also reserved to support future intelligent document processing without exposing sensitive operational data to public cloud services. Evaluation results based on anonymized operational structures and schema-preserving scale tests show that the system processes 500 operational records in 34.26 s. The results also reveal a gap between pre-event preparation completeness and post-event archiving completeness, with Cpre=0.96±0.10 and Carc=0.71±0.32.

title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Electricity Load Levels for Short-Term Energy Management
abstract: With the increasing integration of smart grids and smart meters, vast amounts of consumption data are now available for analysis. Instead of forecasting exact numerical values, classifying electricity demand into discrete load levels can support practical decision-making in demand response, energy management, and tariff optimization. In this paper, a machine learning-based approach presented for classifying electricity consumption into three levels: low, medium, and high. Real residential smart meter data from multiple locations is used, along with time-based and weather-related features. Load levels are assigned using quartile-based thresholds. A variety of classification algorithms, including logistic regression, decision trees, ensemble models, and generalized additive models examined. Random Forest and Bagging classifiers achieve the best performance, with over 87% test accuracy. Confusion matrix analysis and feature importance scores are also provided to support interpretability and robustness. The results demonstrate that machine learning methods can effectively categorize short-term electricity usage, offering a reliable tool for energy-aware planning in smart grid environments.

title: Topology recovery in distribution networks using distance-aware mutual information (DAMI) method
abstract: Topology recovery is crucial for distribution networks, which often experience frequent short-term topology changes, undocumented modifications, incomplete grid observability, or even cyberattacks. Several algorithms that reconstruct network topology based on nodal data have previously been applied to this problem. However, existing approaches typically consider both voltage and power measurements or assume prior knowledge of the network, such as the initial grid topology or zero nodal power correlations. This paper presents a distance-aware, mutual-information-based method for topology recovery in distribution networks using smart meters. We demonstrate, for the first time, that incorporating electrical nodal distances significantly improves the accuracy of mutual-information-based algorithms. Because nodes that are farther apart generally exhibit larger voltage differences, we leverage this property to reweight the mutual information computed from incremental nodal voltages. Given that these incremental voltages follow a Gaussian distribution, voltage correlations can be effectively used to estimate mutual information. The proposed reweighting scheme increases the contribution of pairs with smaller voltage differences while reducing it for those with larger differences. The proposed method, which relies solely on smart meter voltage magnitude data, achieves over 94% accuracy across multiple distribution networks and reduces false or missing line estimations by a factor of two, making it well suited for practical deployment in modern distribution systems.

title: Residential load archetype extraction under low-carbon technology adoption using two-stage DTW meta-clustering
abstract: Understanding household electricity consumption patterns is essential for accurate residential demand modelling, flexibility services, and customer-centric energy interventions. This paper introduces a two-stage clustering framework for half-hourly residential electricity profiles from 495 households in Great Britain, with a sample enriched in low-carbon technology (LCT) adopters. In Stage 1, each household’s 48-point daily net-balance profiles are clustered using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) with a constrained Sakoe–Chiba window. In Stage 2, the resulting 2,511 household-level centroids are re-clustered using DTW to derive 50 cross-household meta-clusters. The proposed approach is benchmarked against Euclidean and unconstrained DTW alternatives. Constrained DTW selected 5.07 clusters per household on average and produced partitions that were distinct from Euclidean clustering (ARI = 0.24 ) while retaining moderate agreement with unconstrained DTW (ARI = 0.71 ). Reconstruction of the clustered profiles achieved range-normalised MAE of 4.0 ± 1.4% at household-centroid level; applying the global meta-clusters to individual households increased this to 5.0 ± 1.8%. At the aggregate level, the constrained-DTW representation produced a range-normalised MAE of 4.7%, with high-demand tiers retaining peaks within the adopted ± 3 h window for 95.5–96.7% of assigned household-days. The constrained DTW implementation required 6.6 times the Euclidean runtime on average, slightly below unconstrained DTW at 6.8 times, while preserving behaviourally interpretable timing features. The resulting archetype library supports demand modelling, flexibility characterisation, and tariff or scheduling studies for LCT-enriched samples.

title: A Latency-Aware Hybrid Computing Architecture for Energy-Latency Optimization in Large-Scale IoT System
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has intensified the challenge of jointly minimizing energy consumption and latency for time-sensitive applications. This paper proposes a latency-aware hybrid IoT-Edge-Cloud computing architecture that dynamically distributes computational tasks across local devices, edge servers, and cloud resources. The proposed framework employs a lightweight and interpretable decision tree-based scheduler, enhanced with K-Means clustering and task dependency awareness, to adapt offloading decisions based on device energy levels, task characteristics, and latency constraints. A multi-tier cost model is formulated to capture the trade-offs between energy consumption and execution delay under Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. Extensive simulations conducted on a large-scale IoT network with 500 devices over 30 independent runs demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach preserves approximately 57% of device energy while maintaining an average task latency of around 325 ms. Compared to local-only and edge-only strategies, the proposed model significantly extends network lifetime while achieving a balanced energy-latency trade-off. These results indicate that the proposed lightweight hybrid architecture is well-suited for scalable and delay-aware IoT applications.

title: A Hybrid CNN–Residual LSTM–Transformer Framework for Multi-Output SCADA Measurement Recovery in Modern Power Systems
abstract: Accurate Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) readings are essential for monitoring modern power grids; however, missing samples and irregular fluctuations often reduce system observability. This paper presents a hybrid deep learning framework, termed Hybrid Stacked Temporal Deep Network (HSTDN), for SCADA data reconstruction and short-term multi-output forecasting of SCADA variables. The architecture integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for local feature extraction, a Residual Stacked Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) module for temporal dependency modeling, and a lightweight Transformer to capture long-range interactions. The proposed approach is evaluated using the IEEE Reliability Test System and real SCADA measurements. Experimental results show that the HSTDN achieves a mean absolute percentage error 0.39% across SCADA output active power, outperforming several benchmark deep learning models. In addition, the unified multi-output structure provides significantly faster inference compared to training and deploying separate models for each variable, making the proposed method suitable for real-time SCADA monitoring and data recovery applications.

title: Federated Learning-Based Cyberattack Detection for Smart Grid Communication Networks
abstract: Abstract False-data injection, denial-of-service, replay, spoofing and other cyberattacks are becoming more common in the smart grid communication networks. Centralized IDS can provide good performance, but it poses issues with data consolidation and privacy and scalability issues. This study introduces a federated intrusion detection framework which is aware of the heterogeneity, named as HA-FedIDS. The framework is based on 15 clients from the public MSU/ORNL power-system security dataset that preserve the sources. The features from physical PMU measurements and cyber-log attributes are fed into two different feature encoders. HA-FedIDS achieved 98.25% accuracy, 96.35% macro-F1, and 99.00% attack recall, with a false-positive rate of 1.83%. It achieved good performance compared to the conventional FedAvg and proximal federated learning, and was close to the centralized performance. Client-wise evaluation also revealed stable detection with non-IID data and decreased participation. The results show that decentralized model averaging is not enough to reliably detect intrusions in the smart-grid. Explicit treatment of client heterogeneity, class imbalance, update instability, and probability calibration improves operational reliability while preserving local data ownership.

title: A 4-D Electrical Feature Fusion Method for Event Detection in Nonintrusive Load Monitoring
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM), a core technology for smart electricity management, heavily relies on reliable front-end event detection for precise load disaggregation. In practice, background noise easily submerges the transient signatures of microloads, causing missed detections. Simultaneously, transient oscillations from ramping nonlinear or cyclic thermostatic loads generate continuous false alarms, severely constraining NILM deployment. To address these challenges, this article proposes a lightweight two-stage event detection method based on 4-D electrical feature fusion. Initially, a 4-D joint feature space comprising active power, reactive power, apparent power, and power factor (PF) (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$P$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$Q$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$S$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-PF) is constructed to dynamically track multidimensional fluctuations via adaptive thresholds. This screening effectively overcomes single-dimensional noise interference, substantially reducing the missed detection rate of microloads. Subsequently, a morphological decoupling algorithm utilizing differential peak prominence is introduced to suppress oscillation-induced false alarms during load ramping, thereby precisely localizing the true state-transition instants of nonlinear events. Furthermore, a time-series macroaggregation strategy is designed to eliminate data redundancy caused by periodic operations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high detection accuracy under complex scenarios, making it highly suitable for real-time edge inference and hardware deployment in residential NILM systems.

title: Digitalization and artificial intelligence for monitoring and optimization of building-integrated photovoltaic systems
abstract: The integration of photovoltaic modules into building envelopes like rooftops, façade and glazing systems is shown to be an effective solution to achieve sustainable energy generation in smart buildings: the Building-Integrated Photovoltaic system. The variability of environmental conditions, partial shading, temperature variations, mismatch losses, and dynamic building energy demand, however, play a significant role on the performance of BIPV systems. In real operating conditions, BIPV systems are nonlinear and stochastic, which can make it difficult to control and optimize the systems. In this context, the applications of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and optimization techniques have become much highlighted to enhance the operational intelligence, reliability and energy efficiency of BIPV infrastructures. For the literature review, the PRISMA method is used in this review to achieve a comprehensive and systematic analysis of machine learning and optimizations techniques applied for smart BIPV systems between 2015 and 2025. The review critically discusses the use of AI in the design of BIPV systems, selection of materials and modules, optimization of design parameters, use of intelligent Maximum Power Point Tracking, energy predictions and building energy management, and fault detection and predictive maintenance. They are compared in terms of prediction accuracy, optimization capability, scalability and practical application with various AI techniques such as Artificial Neural Networks, Deep Learning, Support Vector Machines, Fuzzy Logic Controllers, Genetic Algorithms, and Particle Swarm Optimization. New technologies such as Digital Twins, Internet of Things based monitoring, Cloud and Edge intelligence for intelligent BIPV infrastructures are also addressed in the review. In addition, main research challenges and future research opportunities that can be associated to AI-enabled BIPV systems are systematically identified.

title: SBOA-Inspired Particle Swarm Optimization of XGBoost for False Data Injection Detection in P2P Energy Trading
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading depends on the integrity of smart-meter measurements and coordinator messages. This paper presents an XGBoost detector for false data injection attacks and a hybrid hyperparameter-search mechanism combining particle swarm optimization (PSO) with three hunting-inspired operators from the secretary bird optimization algorithm (SBOA). A common candidate-evaluation budget enables comparison of fixed XGBoost, PSO-XGBoost and SBOA-PSO-XGBoost. The evaluation covers four Austin dataset settings, two attack scenarios and nine classifiers, using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and computational cost. The equal-scenario mean F1 scores are 90.06%, 94.47% and 96.94% for the three XGBoost variants, respectively. The hybrid adds 2.47 percentage points over PSO with a 5.16% increase in total computation time, while its batch-prediction cost remains close to that of PSO-XGBoost. These comparisons characterize the detection-cost trade-off and the role of hybrid search under a shared evaluation protocol.
